gloss: relying on divine help; prayer as a last resort

definitions.gloss: relying on divine help; praying to God as a last resort
definitions.explanation: Turning to the gods or to prayer when all other options have been exhausted. Implies a desperate or helpless situation.

examples.japanese: もう{神頼|かみだの}みしかない。
examples.english: All we can do now is pray.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}{前|まえ}に{神頼|かみだの}みをしても{意味|いみ}がない。
examples.english: Praying before an exam won't do any good.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}もせずに{神頼|かみだの}みばかりしていては{何|なに}も{変|か}わらない。
examples.english: Nothing will change if you just pray without making any effort.

notes:
FORMS:
{神|かみ} (god) + {頼|たの}み (reliance, request). Rendaku changes たのみ to だのみ.

USAGE:
Often used in the expression {神頼|かみだの}みしかない (there's nothing left but to pray). Carries a nuance of desperation — the speaker has tried everything else and has no remaining options. Can also be used critically, to suggest someone is being lazy or passive.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {神頼|かみだの}みをする (to pray to the gods)
- {神頼|かみだの}みしかない (praying is all that's left)
- {最後|さいご}の{神頼|かみだの}み (a last-ditch prayer)
